⟦1⟧, however, fits with ⟦2⟧ 686, and this with ⟦3⟧ 402 and ⟦4⟧ 1025 f. I have already pointed out earlier that the poet presupposes in Athens a kind of democracy, namely the one founded by Theseus (see on 402). 1) See also Weil, Revue des études grecques 1888, p. 12, p. 10*. Now if further, from 685 onward, an archaeology of the Areopagus is given, this agrees with the archaeology of the Delphic prologue, and indeed also in character insofar as here and there the legends that reported strife between gods are set aside. The legend of the Areopagus is given by Euripides, who certainly did not invent it, ⟦5⟧, I.T. 945 ff.: ⟦6⟧ is named from the fact that Ares, who had killed Halirrhothios, son of Poseidon, was judged here by the gods themselves. In place of this Aeschylus sets the legend of the Amazons, who as daughters of Ares had sacrificed to him here, and here he perhaps innovates, since nowhere else does the Areopagus appear as occupied and fortified by the Amazons. On the battles between Athenians and Amazons, from which panegyric rhetoric as well as the plastic and pictorial arts so gladly took material, Plutarch treats precisely in Theseus ch. 27, especially after Cleidemus; according to him the Amazons had their camp in the region of the Pnyx, which is at least adjacent to the Areopagus, but one reads nothing of a foundation of a city, even if the battles lasted some months. Yet Stanley cites Etym. M. ⟦7⟧ and Eustath. on Dionys. Perieg. 653, where the name is derived from the fact that the Amazons, daughters of Ares, had come there on their expedition (thus somewhat differently than here). What Aeschylus actually says, however, must first be examined. The sentence beginning with ⟦8⟧ runs anacoluthically, and one cannot even see on what, according to the first intention, this accusative should depend; since now also the name ⟦9⟧ is explained only at 690, where it occurs again, it has been conjectured that the first time it crept in erroneously, in place of the verb or participle governing the accusative. Nearest at hand is ⟦10⟧, from which the corruption could easily arise; cf. ⟦11⟧ ⟦12⟧, ⟦13⟧ (⟦14⟧ pointing to the present appearance).
